title: a `neural_block` descriptor declaring the `accumulate` terminal-write contract is accepted by the shared validator, refused at every launching door
why: `accumulate` is a second terminal-write contract alongside `unique_write`:
it declares that a target may legitimately be written by more than one
source per step, with the committed result being an order-unspecified sum.
The underlying mechanism (atomic add, block-reduce, and so on) stays
internal and is never part of the wire format; only the contract name is,
and this fixture is that value's structural-acceptance check — the actual
executor behaviour is a separate concern from whether the descriptor
The fixture is otherwise identical to row01's golden with only
`scatter_policy` changed from `unique_write` to `accumulate`, so the only
thing exercised is that this value is actually accepted, not merely absent
from the disallowed/dead-spelling sets checked elsewhere.
Accepted at the shared validator, for the same reason as row01: the
descriptor is structurally valid schema v1. Refused at the
manifest-bypassing plugin loader, with the same message and reasoning as
row01: a `neural_block` descriptor is recognized but never
launch-certified, regardless of which terminal-write contract it declares.
